author: Skquid
body:
JapaneseSquid's, real name Sean, Staff application for Avicus network, 3/14/17, 7:02 PM EST

Age: 15
Timezone: EST, USA
Teamspeak?: Possible, but at the moment, no.
Skype? Yes.
Recording software? Yes.


CRITEREA 1
Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?
For major servers,(such as hypixel and mineplex) no, but in PvP servers with around 1000 people, yes, around 4 months, but those servers have long since shut down.
What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?
My biggest weakness is probably my temper, seeing toxic players and or cocky hackers boil me up a bit too easily, especially last year. However, I don't experience as much now, as I have learned to cope with it.
My strength is most likely my experience with hackers, and how I can tell legitimate to non legitimate. I have developed this in my former experiences in other servers.
How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?
I believe I can help the staff team by adding another individual to look out for hackers and/or overly toxic players. I can also help make tough decisions on if one is hacking using recording software and my past encounters with them.
What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?
A leader needs to be decisive. A leader needs to know how they can help bring their community to a better level, and be the one that others look up to to save them. I consider myself a leader, as I have been able to find a common ground between 2 opposing sides, and observe very precisely on a situation to make a tough decision.
What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
My attributes that distinguish myself from others are mainly focused on an equal playing ground. I have always been trying to make things equal for everybody, and have exercised many procedures on ways to make a community great, on my past experiences with unbalanced and/or corrupted communities. My passion is mainly to be somebody that can help the common person and reinforce rules and regulations.
What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?
Skills in which I believe are essential in interactions with the community are finding a happy medium, enforcing laws, and maintaining a good reputation with the community. I believe I do have these skills, as I have mentioned briefly before, that I can interact and lead a community to the best of their interests and finding a compromise in 2 opposing sides. My passion and push to maintain a good community can help within enforcing the rules.
How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 
Most likely around 5 years, possibly more, depending on how life goes.
CITEREA 2
You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?
First of all, I would record them immediately. I would upload those recordings to the forums later. In order to help the players at that time and prevent furthermore unfairness, If I had already been granted privileges I would ban them depending on the rules at that time. If any staff or players are skeptical of my decision, they can always view the recordings on the forums. If, however, the decision is very unclear, I would most likely temp ban them and seek counsel form senior moderators later on. The same process with the recording is applicable once more.
Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?
I would support which side I believe is correct, and make a group decision on what we should do about the staff member. In this case, I would most likely support the other staff members and try to decide, together as a whole, on what to do with the member. 
A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realise that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?
If there is no proof, and I know very well that the player is a rule breaker, I will try my best to to the following:
1. See if any other staff members/players have proof.
2. If no proof is found, observe the player's profile and statistics.
3. Any suspicious statistics or profile information is collected and or recorded.
4. Appeal the ban.
5. Place close attention/monitor the player for around 2 weeks after.
6. If any other infractions are made, place all proof collected together and ban them, noting the player was banned before and that it has been appealed. 
(Funny thing is, I tried reporting a player before, and my file got corrupted, luckily a staff took care of the situation)
You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?
I would let the staff know about their potential violation, and try my best to eliminate the screenshot. I would warn the staff member of his/her mistake and tell another mod about the situation.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?
I would do the following:
1. Ask for all information regarding the situation.
2. Observe the details, and brainstorm my perspective.
3. If my opposition stands, create a post explaining my opposition, and ask for any feedback.
4. Politely as the staff to review and revise their decision, and suggest a compromise in between.
5. If nothing changes, and it seems as though their decision stands, accept their choice and standpoint, and know that there is no way in which I can always get what I would like. If any staff ask for my reasoning, I would answer in the most civilized way possible.
CRITERIA 3
What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?
Being an Avicus moderator is very important to me. I spend most, if not all my hours of Minecraft into advices, and knowing that I can create the server that I love into a better community is probably the best that it can get.

How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?
As mentioned above, Avicus is my most favorite server, and 90% of my Minecraft time is spent there. Avicus is very important as I was there since the days of MCzone. It was my 3rd server ever, and the best one I could possibly thing of.

Do you speak any other languages than English?
I speak fluent Japanese, although it would most likely be obsolete to the community.

Do you have anything else to add to your application?
Yes. I have recently been able to get more access to Avicus, and so my activity will be in my personal peak position for as long as anything does not interrupt or intercept it.
